fact_check.claim: In a New York building with four or more residential units, landlord consent to a sublease cannot be unreasonably withheld
fact_check.note: RPL 226-b(2)(a): 'Such consent shall not be unreasonably withheld'; applies to a dwelling having four or more residential units.

fact_check.claim: Request goes by certified mail, return receipt requested, with term, subtenant name and addresses, reason, tenant's address during sublet, co-tenant/guarantor written consent, copy of sublease
fact_check.note: Section 2(b) lists these items.

fact_check.claim: Landlord has 10 days to ask for more information
fact_check.note: Section 2(c): within ten days after mailing, the landlord may ask for additional information. Also stated in the Cornell Law guide.

fact_check.claim: Landlord must respond within 30 days of the request or of the extra information, whichever is later; silence is deemed consent
fact_check.note: Section 2(c) gives 30 days running from the later mailing; failure to send notice is deemed consent. The Cornell Law guide says the same.

fact_check.claim: Original tenant remains liable under the lease after subletting
fact_check.note: Section 2(c): tenant 'shall nevertheless remain liable for the performance of tenant's obligations'. Cornell Law guide also says tenant remains financially responsible.

fact_check.claim: Subletting without consent is a 'substantial breach of lease or tenancy'
fact_check.note: Section 5 uses that phrase for noncompliant sublets or assignments.

fact_check.claim: Lease provisions waiving the section are void
fact_check.note: Section 6: any provision purporting to waive is null and void.

fact_check.claim: Statute excludes public housing and co-op proprietary leases
fact_check.note: Section 3 excludes public housing and other units with statutory admission criteria, and proprietary leases.

fact_check.claim: Bad-faith landlord can owe the tenant's legal costs; if refusal is unreasonable the tenant may sublet anyway
fact_check.note: Section 2(c) allows costs and attorneys' fees on a bad-faith finding. The 'may sublet anyway' clause was not in the excerpt the fetch returned, but it matches my reading of the statute's section 2(d); acceptable.

fact_check.claim: Owner may refuse an assignment without giving a reason; the remedy for unreasonable refusal is release on 30 days' notice
fact_check.note: Section 1: consent to assignment 'may be unconditionally withheld without cause'; if unreasonable, owner must release tenant on 30 days notice, as the sole remedy. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Buildings with three or fewer units: the lease controls; subsidized apartments excluded
fact_check.note: Guide section 3.4 says the right to sublease is controlled by the lease in 3-or-fewer-unit buildings, and the sublet laws do not apply to government-subsidized apartments.

fact_check.claim: Reasonable refusal: lease stays in force and tenant still owes remaining rent
fact_check.note: Guide: you cannot proceed with the sublease and the lease continues, so you remain responsible for rent. The article's example ('such as skipping the notice procedure') is the writer's illustration, not the source's.

fact_check.claim: Landlord may charge background/credit check fee but not sublet fees not listed in the lease; a listed fee must be reasonable
fact_check.note: Matches the Fees paragraph of the guide.

fact_check.claim: Article states no usual Ithaca sublet fee could be sourced and gives no dollar figure
fact_check.note: Previous fix applied; no unsourced figure appears. A $250 fee seen in a search snippet from a landlord page was not added, correctly, because that page would not load for me.

fact_check.claim: With an assignment you are not liable if the new tenant fails to pay; mutual termination is an option
fact_check.note: Guide says assigning ends your agreement and you are not liable for the new tenant; names mutual termination agreement as an option.

fact_check.claim: Tenants Advocacy Program hotline 607-301-1560
fact_check.note: Number appears on the page.

fact_check.claim: Off-Campus Living phone 607-255-2310; lease checklist lists 'ability to sublet' and 'conditions for sublet'
fact_check.note: Both appear on the page (Termination heading and contact line).

fact_check.claim: Marketplace visible and contactable only by Cornell-affiliated people or those who can prove it
fact_check.note: Page says so.

fact_check.claim: Off-Campus Living email list is a forum for subletting, open to the Cornell community with a NetID
fact_check.note: Page says so.

fact_check.claim: Cornell lists Daily Sun, Ithacarents.com, Ithaca Journal, Ithaca Times, does not endorse them; Ithacarents only lets Landlords Association of Tompkins County members post
fact_check.note: All confirmed. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Cornell advises viewing properties in person and reading the whole lease before signing or paying
fact_check.note: Page says so.

fact_check.claim: Marketplace has a Subleases section and a 'List/Find Sublets' option
fact_check.note: Nav bar has Subleases; banner lists List/Find Sublets.

fact_check.claim: Grad School: marketplace free to use for those with Cornell credentials, particularly helpful for grad students who want to sublet
fact_check.note: Page says it costs nothing for people with Cornell credentials and is 'particularly helpful for graduate students'. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Step 2: some landlords may require student subtenants or the same screening (flagged as an example to ask about, not a finding)
fact_check.note: Hedged with 'may' and labeled as unverified, so it is not presented as a hard fact. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Public sites reach more people and more scammers (labeled 'Our view')
fact_check.note: Labeled as the writer's opinion. Previous fix applied.

beats_top.query: cornell summer sublet how to sublet apartment ithaca landlord permission
beats_top.why: The top results are an old 2008 Cornell Sun listing, a Craigslist post, landlord pages and short Cornell guidance. The most substantive source, the Law School guide, covers sublets as one section of a long lease-breaking page. Ours answers up front, with the 4-unit rule, the 10-day and 30-day clock, a request checklist, fees, where to list and scam advice.
changes: Optional: if an Ithaca landlord's official tenant page states a sublet fee or student-only rule, link it and add the figure.
Optional: add a short template letter for the certified-mail request.
